object.start: Ask the daemon to start it, on the nodes its placement elects.
object.stop: Ask the daemon to stop all its instances; it stays stopped.
object.restart: Ask the daemon to restart its instances.
object.freeze: Block the automatic starts and the monitor actions of the daemon, on all its nodes.
object.unfreeze: Let the daemon start it and act on it again.
object.switch: Stop the running instance and start it on the next preferred node.
object.giveback: Stop the misplaced instances and start them on the preferred nodes.
object.enable: Act on it again: the actions no longer skip it.
object.disable: Skip it on the actions; what runs is left as it is.
object.provision: Allocate the system resources its resources need on its nodes: format a filesystem, create a volume…
object.unprovision: Free the system resources of its resources on all its nodes: their data is lost.
object.delete: Delete its configuration from the cluster; its system resources are left in place.
object.purge: Unprovision, then delete it: its data and its configuration are lost.

instance.start: Bring up the instance resources on this node.
instance.stop: Bring down the instance resources on this node.
instance.restart: Restart the instance on this node.
instance.run: Run its tasks now, outside their schedule.
instance.boot: Run the clean up actions done at node boot only.
instance.shutdown: Stop the instance, its standby resources too, as on a node shutdown.
instance.startStandby: Activate the resources meant to stay up on a standby node.
instance.freeze: Block the automatic starts and the monitor actions on this node.
instance.unfreeze: Unblock the automatic starts and the monitor actions on this node.
instance.clear: Clear the failed state of its monitor, for the daemon to act on it again.
instance.provision: Allocate the system resources of its resources on this node.
instance.unprovision: Free the system resources of its resources on this node: their data is lost.
instance.install: Install again what its volumes and filesystems declare, without starting anything.
instance.prstart: Preempt the exclusive write reservation of its devices.
instance.prstop: Release the exclusive write reservation of its devices.
instance.syncUpdate: Copy the changes of the local dataset to the peers.
instance.syncFull: Copy the whole local dataset to the peers.
instance.syncResync: Restore the optimal synchronization of the replicated pairs.
instance.syncSplit: Make both ends of a replicated pair read-write.
instance.syncIngest: Ingest the files received from the active instance.
instance.pgReset: Lift the process group cappings, whatever the pg_* keywords say.
instance.pgUpdate: Apply the pg_* keywords to the process groups again.
instance.info: Gather and show the instance information.
instance.status: Evaluate the status of its resources again.
instance.delete: Delete the instance configuration on this node.
instance.syncUpdateStore: Back up the changes of its datasets into their stores.
instance.syncUpdateEither: Copy the changes of its datasets to the peers, or back them up into their stores.
instance.syncFullStore: Back up its whole datasets into their stores.
instance.syncFullEither: Copy its whole datasets to the peers, or back them up into their stores.
instance.unstop: Lower the flags a stop raised on the instance, starting nothing: the daemon may start it again on its own.

resource.run: Run the tasks picked now, outside their schedule.
resource.console: Open a console in the container.
resource.startStandby: Bring up the resources picked meant to stay up on a standby node.

clusterLocks.intro: The locks the node speaking for the cluster granted, whose holder has neither released them nor seen their lease end, as om cluster lock list shows them. A lock serializes what reads the state of the cluster and changes it on the strength of that reading.

clusterLocks.stale: Not read again ({{message}}): the locks below are as last read, none released until they are read again.

acquire.title: Acquire a cluster lock

acquire.warning: A lock held here holds every client of the cluster asking it: release it once done, or keep its lease short.

pages.cluster: This is your cluster at a glance. A cluster is a group of servers (nodes) that watch each other and keep your applications running: if one node fails, its applications restart on another. Each card below summarizes a page of the menu; click it to open that page.
pages.heartbeats: Nodes send each other small messages, called heartbeats, to show they are alive. Each node both sends (tx) and receives (rx), over several paths in case one breaks. If a node goes silent on every path, the others treat it as failed and can restart its applications.
pages.nodes: These are the servers in your cluster. Each one runs the OpenSVC agent. Their load and free memory help decide where applications run. A frozen node is left alone: the cluster will not start or move anything on it automatically.
pages.namespaces: Namespaces group objects, like folders. An object's full name is namespace/kind/name, for example prod/svc/web. You can grant access per namespace, and limit how much storage, CPU, memory and IP addresses it may use.
pages.networks: These are the networks the cluster uses to give IP addresses to containers and services automatically.
pages.pools: Storage pools are where volumes get their disk space: a directory, an LVM volume group, a ZFS pool or a storage array, for example.
pages.stores: Backup stores hold copies (snapshots) of your services' data and configuration, so you can restore them later, even on another node.
pages.resources: This lists every resource of every service and volume, on every node: filesystems, IP addresses, disks, containers, applications. Problems only keeps what is down or in warn, leaving out the passive nodes of a failover service, down as they should be.
pages.objects-services: Services (svc) are the applications the cluster keeps running. Each one is built from resources, such as an IP address, a filesystem and a container. A service has one instance on each node it is allowed to run on.
pages.objects-volumes: Volumes (vol) are storage that a service asks for. The cluster creates each volume in a storage pool when the service is provisioned.
pages.objects-configs: Configurations (cfg) hold settings and files that are not secret. Services use them as files or environment variables. The cluster's own configuration is listed here too.
pages.objects-secrets: Secrets (sec) are like configurations, but stored encrypted. Use them for passwords, certificates and private keys.
pages.objects-users: Users (usr) are accounts that can sign in to this webapp and the API, each with its own permissions (grants).
pages.objects-any: All the objects in the cluster, of every kind: services, volumes, configurations, secrets and users.

groups.concepts: What a cluster is made of

cluster.definition: A group of servers (nodes) that share one configuration and watch each other. If a node fails, the applications it was running can restart on another node.

node.definition: One server in the cluster. It runs the OpenSVC agent, and the applications (instances) the cluster places on it.

object.definition: Anything the cluster manages: a service, a volume, a configuration, a secret or a user. Its full name is namespace/kind/name, for example prod/svc/web.

instance.definition: One copy of an object on one node. A service allowed on two nodes has two instances; usually only one is running. Each instance has its own status.

resource.definition: One building block of an object: an IP address, a filesystem, a disk, a container, an application, a backup job… Its name says its type and number, for example fs#1 is the first filesystem.

namespace.definition: A folder for objects. Permissions and limits are set per namespace. The default one is root; system holds the cluster's own objects.

kinds.definition: The type of an object: svc (service), vol (volume), cfg (configuration), sec (secret), usr (user), nscfg (namespace settings) or ccfg (cluster settings).

heartbeat.definition: A stream of small "I'm alive" messages between nodes. Each node sends (tx) and receives (rx). If a node stays silent longer than the timeout, the others treat it as failed.

relay.definition: A heartbeat that goes through a third server acting as a mailbox. Useful when the nodes cannot reach each other directly, or as an extra safety path.

network.definition: A network the cluster gives IP addresses from, automatically, to services and containers that ask for one.

pool.definition: A place volumes get their disk space from: a directory, an LVM volume group, ZFS, DRBD or a storage array.

store.definition: A place backups are kept. Every node can reach it, so a backup taken on one node can be restored on another.

snapshot.definition: One backup: a copy of a service's data and configuration at a point in time, with the node that took it. The store keeps a limited number of them.

label.definition: A tag on a node, like az=fr2. Services can use labels to choose which nodes they run on.

kindSvc.definition: A service: an application the cluster keeps running, made of resources such as an IP address, filesystems and containers.

kindVol.definition: A volume: storage for a service, created in a storage pool and attached to the service that asked for it.

kindCfg.definition: A configuration: settings and files that are not secret, given to services as files or environment variables.

kindSec.definition: A secret: like a configuration, but stored encrypted. For passwords, certificates and keys.

kindUsr.definition: A user: an account for the API and this webapp, with its permissions. Not needed for people who sign in with OpenID.

kindNscfg.definition: The settings of a namespace: for example the maximum storage, CPU, memory and IP addresses its objects may use.

kindCcfg.definition: The cluster's own settings, shared by every node. There is only one.

avail.definition: Is it running? Only the resources it needs count. up: running. down: not running. warn: partly running, or running in too many places. stdby up: only the standby resources run. n/a: nothing to run.

overall.definition: The full health check: like Avail, but every resource and every warning counts. Overall can be warn while Avail is up: it works, but something needs a look.

provisioned.definition: Whether the system pieces it needs (filesystems, disks, volumes) have been created on the node. mixed means only some of them.

frozen.definition: The cluster leaves it alone: no automatic start, stop or move. You can still run actions yourself.

monitor.definition: What the cluster is doing with it right now. idle means nothing; starting, stopping or provisioning means an action is in progress; a value like start failed tells you an action failed.

expect.definition: The state the cluster is working towards. With a > in front, it was asked for the whole cluster (for example >started); without, it is this node keeping the instance running.

globalExpect.definition: The goal of a cluster-wide action someone asked for, such as started, stopped or placed. Every instance works towards it until it is reached.

localExpect.definition: What this node keeps the instance at. started means the node restarts it if it fails.

orchestration.definition: A cluster-wide action in progress, such as starting a service on its preferred node. All the instances involved share its id until it is done.

standby.definition: A resource kept running even on nodes where the service is not, so it is ready to take over (for example, receiving replicated data).

encap.definition: A resource managed from inside a container, by an agent running in it, instead of by the node.

optional.definition: A resource whose failure is not fatal: actions continue and the service still counts as up. Its problems show in Overall.

monitored.definition: A resource the cluster watches closely. If it fails and cannot be restarted, the cluster reacts: it switches the service to another node, or reboots the node.

leader.definition: The node that speaks for the cluster: the first one in the node list that is alive. It handles cluster-wide tasks. It has nothing to do with where services run.

score.definition: How much spare capacity a node has, based on its load and free memory. Higher means freer. Services can be placed on the node with the highest score.

overloaded.definition: The node's free memory or swap is below the minimum set in its configuration.

topology.definition: How many copies of a service may run at the same time. failover: only one, on one node. flex: several at once, between a minimum and a maximum.

orchestrate.definition: How much the cluster acts on its own. no: never starts or moves the service. start: starts it once after a node boots. ha: high availability, restarts it on another node when its node fails.

placement.definition: How the cluster picks the node a service runs on: the first node listed (nodes order), the least loaded, the highest score, spread across nodes, and so on.

flex.definition: For a flex service: the minimum and maximum number of copies that may run, and the target number the cluster aims for.

actionProvision.definition: Create what the service needs on its nodes: its filesystems, disks and volumes.

actionUnprovision.definition: Delete what provision created: the filesystems are wiped and the disks released. The data is lost; the configuration is kept.

actionFreeze.definition: Tell the cluster to leave something alone: no automatic start, stop or move. Works on a service, a node or the whole cluster.

actionUnfreeze.definition: Undo a freeze: the cluster acts automatically again.

actionSwitch.definition: Move a running service to another node: it stops here and starts on the next preferred node, or on the node you choose.

actionTakeover.definition: Move a running service to this node: it stops where it runs and starts here.

actionGiveback.definition: Move services back to their preferred nodes, for example after a failure has been fixed.

actionDrain.definition: Empty a node before maintenance: freeze it, then stop everything running on it. Services in high availability (ha) can then start on other nodes.

actionPurge.definition: Delete the service completely: its data and system resources, then its configuration on every node. This cannot be undone.

actionAbort.definition: Cancel the cluster-wide action in progress.

actionClear.definition: Reset a failed state (such as start failed) so the cluster acts on it again.

states.warn: Warning: running, but something needs your attention.
states.down: Down: not running, and it should be.
states.downQuiet: Down, as expected. For example, the standby node of a failover service.
states.na: Not applicable: there is nothing to run here.
states.undef: Unknown: the node has not reported this yet.

marks.overallWarn: Some of its resources have a warning.
marks.running: A task or sync is running right now.
marks.rpoBreached: Its last backup or replication is older than allowed (RPO breached).
marks.drp: Disaster recovery node: used only when the main site is lost.
marks.leader: Preferred node: where the service runs when everything is normal.
marks.leaderNonOptimal: Preferred node, but the service is not running where placement wants it. A giveback moves it back.
marks.frozen: Frozen: the cluster will not start, stop or move it automatically.
marks.stopped: Stopped on purpose by an operator: the cluster will not restart it.
marks.notProvisioned: Not provisioned: its filesystems, disks or volumes are not created on this node.

flags.R: R, running: a task or sync of this resource is running now.
flags.M: M, monitored: if it fails, the cluster reacts (switches the service, or reboots the node).
flags.D: D, disabled: every action skips it.
flags.O: O, optional: if it fails, the service still counts as up.
flags.E: E, encapsulated: managed from inside a container.
flags.S: S, standby: kept running even on nodes where the service is not running.
flags.P: P, not provisioned on this node.
flags.X: X, stopped on purpose by an operator.
flags.restarts: A number: how many automatic restarts are left before the cluster gives up.

about.tagline: The webapp of an OpenSVC cluster: watch and drive its nodes, its objects and their resources.

licenses.title: Licenses and sources
licenses.bundled: This webapp bundles the following software, each under its own license:

privacy.title: Personal data (GDPR)
privacy.none: This webapp collects nothing for OpenSVC SAS: no analytics, no tracking, no advertising. It talks to the API of this cluster alone.
privacy.controller: The cluster is run by your organization, the controller of the data it records, such as who signed in and the actions done.
privacy.browser: Your browser keeps on this device, in its local storage: your sign-in tokens, removed when you sign out; a cached summary of the cluster; your display preferences. Clearing the site data of your browser removes them all.
privacy.github: On your say-so only, your user page asks GitHub, at most once an hour, for the latest release of this webapp: that request reaches GitHub with your address. Off by default.
privacy.oidc: Signed in through an OpenID provider, its own policy applies to what it handles.
privacy.rights: For your rights over the data the cluster records, ask its operator; for this software, write to <mail/>.
privacy.releaseCheck: Check GitHub for the latest release of this webapp
